root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation of steadfast attachment, abiding connection, and persistence.
root_idea.development: The attached or abiding relation is concretized in وَتِين as a vital vessel closely associated with the heart. A related derived usage extends the image to close approach or proximity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized singular nominal citation form وَتِين.

senses.definition: A vital great artery or vein associated with the heart and supplying the liver and other tissues; it is described variously as the aorta, a vessel along the backbone, or the heart’s khilb, that is, its niyāṭ. Severing it is fatal.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic use, it occurs in the definite expression الْوَتِينَ in 69:46, where cutting it is presented as a fatal act. Classical anatomical descriptions vary in their identification of the precise vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose watin has been severed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived designation formed from the anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Close approach or drawing near to someone, likened to the close attachment of the watin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived conventional usage expressing proximity rather than the anatomical vessel itself.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Its anatomical descriptions and fatal-severing association are covered by the Quranic sense.
The alternative identification with the khilb or heart’s niyāṭ is covered within the same anatomical sense.

cautions: Classical anatomical descriptions differ on whether the watin is identified specifically as the aorta, another major vein or artery, or a vessel associated with the heart and backbone.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The final Mufradat clause records a camel-related form as اسْتَوْطَنَ, whose ط formally indicates the separate root و-ط-ن rather than canonical و-ت-ن; its meaning is therefore not assigned to this root.
